an5.42:1.1: “Bhikkhus, when a good person is born in a family, it is for the good, welfare, and happiness of many people.
an5.42:1.2: It is for the good, welfare, and happiness of (1) his mother and father,
an5.42:2.1: Just as a great rain cloud, nurturing all the crops, appears for the good, welfare, and happiness of many people,
an5.42:2.2: so too, when a good person is born in a family, it is for the good, welfare, and happiness of many people.
an5.42:2.3: It is for the good, welfare, and happiness of his mother and father …
an5.42:3.1: The deities protect one guarded by the Dhamma,
an5.42:3.2: who has managed his wealth for the welfare of many.
an5.42:3.3:
Fame does not forsake one steadfast in the Dhamma,
who is learned and of virtuous behavior and observances.
an5.42:3.4:
Who is fit to blame him,
standing in Dhamma,
an5.42:4.2:
a speaker of truth,
possessing a sense of shame,
an5.42:4.3: pure like a coin of refined gold?
an5.42:4.6: by Brahmā, too, he is praised.
